unsupported_claims: Alias table preprocessing cost grows with the sum of squared degrees, so denser graphs make preprocessing considerably more expensive (the paper calls preprocessing negligibly small; this is not in the evidence)
Speed comes from C/Python word2vec-style implementations (not stated in the evidence)
rationale: The answer does not accept the false premise, saying it cannot confirm Barabási-Albert graphs. However, it never states the correction (Erdos-Renyi graphs, constant degree 10), and it adds claims about preprocessing cost and implementation that the evidence does not support. The evidence actually says preprocessing is negligible. The claims about linear scaling in node count and parallelism are supported.
